title: selfcheck's host check, and the review's done before its whole-suite run, name a host too loaded for the suite to meet its seconds ceiling
goal: selfcheck's host check fails when the 5-minute load average is over SUITE_LOAD_PER_CORE times the cores, the per-core load at which a whole-suite tests.py run no longer fits its darwin seconds ceiling (value: gate load), whatever LOAD_PER_CORE allows (seen in the SP-wwacrsqr review, where selfcheck passed at a load near 10 on 14 cores while another application held the CPU); a review story's done refuses with the host named, before it starts a whole-suite tests.py run, at such a load (that run took 168 s against the 22 s ceiling and refused after three minutes)

clauses.clause: selfcheck's host check fails when the 5-minute load average is over SUITE_LOAD_PER_CORE times the cores, the per-core load at which a whole-suite tests.py run no longer fits its darwin seconds ceiling (value: gate load), whatever LOAD_PER_CORE allows (seen in the SP-wwacrsqr review, where selfcheck passed at a load near 10 on 14 cores while another application held the CPU)
a review story's done refuses with the host named, before it starts a whole-suite tests.py run, at such a load (that run took 168 s against the 22 s ceiling and refused after three minutes)

gates.question: At what 5-minute load average per core does a host count as too loaded for a whole-suite tests.py run to meet its darwin seconds limit, so selfcheck's host check fails and a review story's done refuses before it starts that run?
options: 0.5 per core (7 on 14 cores): SUITE_LOAD_PER_CORE of _tools/bl_selfcheck.py is 0.5 and done reads it too; it names the load near 10 of the SP-wwacrsqr review and no load of 2 to 5, at which the suite passed on a rerun in the closes
0.25 per core (3.5 on 14 cores): also refuses at the load of 3 to 5 at which the suite passed on a rerun in the closes
1.0 per core (14 on 14 cores): names only a host far past the load of 10 of the SP-wwacrsqr review
gates.recommendation: 0.5 per core (7 on 14 cores): SUITE_LOAD_PER_CORE of _tools/bl_selfcheck.py is 0.5 and done reads it too; it names the load near 10 of the SP-wwacrsqr review and no load of 2 to 5, at which the suite passed on a rerun in the closes
gates.answer: 0.5 per core (7 on 14 cores): SUITE_LOAD_PER_CORE of _tools/bl_selfcheck.py is 0.5 and done reads it too; it names the load near 10 of the SP-wwacrsqr review and no load of 2 to 5, at which the suite passed on a rerun in the closes
gates.host_unchecked: the gate picks a per-core load threshold the code carries (SUITE_LOAD_PER_CORE), not a host setup to prove; the host's load changes minute to minute, so no host command proves the answer, and the item's own test plants the load

notes: Premise run 2026-10-12: bl_selfcheck.check_host(load=10.0, cores=14) returns state ok (LOAD_PER_CORE 1.5 puts its limit at 21), so a host at the load of the SP-wwacrsqr review passes selfcheck today. The refusal would not fire now: the 5-minute load of the planning host is 3.3 on 14 cores, under the 7 the gate load answer sets. Where the test goes, decided at planning (the suite is at 100 of 100 ids): the check's selector names a test that does not exist yet, so the worker renames test_backlog_selfcheck_young_distill_run_is_a_hook_in_flight_and_an_old_stray_process_still_fails in _tools/test_backlog_portable.py by appending _and_selfcheck_host_load_suite_ceiling (appended, so the selector of ST-y6syvkzo still matches), extends it with a check_host planted load and the done refusal's own helper read with a planted load, and adds no id; the one test covers both goal clauses. Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 14 of 19, "The whole suite fits its seconds ceiling under host load without the ceiling changing"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates. SP-e4fm2ovk close (2026-10-13): five of six workers saw whole-suite runs pass all 100 tests yet exit 1 on the darwin 24 s ceiling (24.4 to 39 s) with sibling workers on the host; each reran once and passed or named the known bugs. Correction to the line above: five of the sprint's seven workers, not five of six. Recurred in SP-u5q37ds3 (2026-10-13): workers of BG-zsiguf72, ST-ra7u7hwd and BG-xvvclquq saw whole-suite runs of 24-31 s against the 24 s darwin ceiling while a sibling held the host test lock; each passed on a rerun.
